correctness.rationale: Exact four-parameter Jacobian yields the displayed station Gram products. Rotational conjugacy and strict log-det concavity upper-bound every common-radius station arrangement by its isotropized Fisher matrix; vanishing first and second angular moments characterize equality, and regular polygons attain it for every n>=3. The determinant has positive factors and reduces to g(z)=z(1+5z/2)^2/(1+z)^14; its derivative has one positive quadratic zero, giving the stated unique global radius. Direct execution of check.py verified symbolic square/triangle information matrices, determinant, angular counterexample and derivative/root. Finite checks are supporting only, not proof of all designs.

originality.rationale: The exact common-ring optimum with necessary-and-sufficient angular moment conditions and closed algebraic radius was not found in the substantive primary material inspected or the targeted mathematical search results. Prior work establishes the forward model, nonlinear inversion, station-network simulations and general design ideas, but no checked prior result was shown to imply the whole theorem. A related Mogi source result concerns peak splitting in superposed scalar displacement, not 4-parameter Fisher information. The conclusion is a best-knowledge originality judgment with unresolved specialized-source risk.

value.rationale: Four-parameter source inversion is physically motivated by actual GPS monitoring, where depth/strength and horizontal position are coupled. The result gives an exact angular balance characterization for every station count n>=3 and a unique dimensionless optimal radius, not an arbitrary unmotivated numerical instance. It can benchmark network-planning methods under an interpretable idealization while clearly limiting all claims to local equal-noise ring designs.
